the והתניא of 40b.14: one who vows off the fruits of the land
anonymous redactorial voice: למימרא ... והתניא, והא ... קתני, תני

props.gloss_en: over a thing whose growth is not from the ground, e.g. the flesh of cattle, beasts, fowl and fish, one says 'by Whose word all things came to be'
over milk, eggs and cheese one says shehakol
over mouldy bread, wine gone sour and a cooked dish whose form has spoiled one says shehakol
over salt and brine one says shehakol
over truffles and mushrooms one says shehakol
one who vows off the fruits of the land is permitted truffles and mushrooms; if he said 'all growths of the ground are upon me', he is forbidden even truffles and mushrooms
Abaye: in growing, they grow from the ground; in drawing sustenance, they do not draw from the ground
teach [the baraita's opening clause as]: over a thing that does not draw sustenance from the ground

objections.gloss_en: למימרא דכמהין ופטריות לאו גידולי קרקע נינהו? והתניא: ... כל גידולי קרקע עלי -- אסור אף בכמהין ופטריות -- the vow baraita counts them as growths of the ground, yet this baraita lists them under what does not grow from the ground

answered_by.gloss_en: מירבא רבו מארעא, מינק לא ינקי מארעא -- they grow from the ground but draw no sustenance from it (= p_abaye_mirba_ravu)

objections.gloss_en: והא 'על דבר שאין גדולו מן הארץ' קתני! -- the baraita's own words are 'whose GROWTH is not from the ground', and by Abaye they do grow from it

answered_by.gloss_en: תני: על דבר שאין יונק מן הארץ -- emend the clause to 'does not draw sustenance from the ground' (= p_tni_ein_yonek)
